title: wifi signal not updateing
author: anto605
summary: The report is too underspecified to route today: it says a PowerToys docking option does not update Wi-Fi signal status, but it does not identify which PowerToys feature or UI surface actually shows that status.

judgment.rationale: Before maintainers can triage this as a PowerToys bug, the reporter needs to identify the exact PowerToys surface and transition where the stale Wi-Fi status appears.
evidence: The issue is labeled only as a general bug and does not carry a product-area label.
The body says powertoys docking option is not updating Wi-Fi signal status, but it never identifies the specific PowerToys feature, page, or tray surface involved.
No screenshot, bug-report ZIP, or follow-up comments are attached.
A focused repository search did not reveal an obvious built-in Wi-Fi signal status surface that maps unambiguously to the report text.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to identify the exact PowerToys surface, show the stale Wi-Fi state, and describe the trigger that should update it.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete PowerToys code fix can be scoped until the reporter identifies which PowerToys feature or surface is allegedly displaying the stale Wi-Fi status.

issue_context.summary: The current report says a PowerToys docking option is not updating Wi-Fi status on a Dell machine, but it does not identify the module or UI surface where that status is shown.
known_information: The report is on PowerToys 0.100.2, installed per-user and running non-elevated on Windows 10 19044.
The Area field is General rather than a product-specific module.
No attachments or comments are present.
The only hardware detail supplied is a Dell M4700 laptop mention in the repro text.
inferences: The problem may refer to a dock-related UI or workflow, but the current wording is too ambiguous to map to a single PowerToys module.
Without a screenshot or exact surface name, the issue could be a misunderstanding of a non-PowerToys UI rather than a PowerToys bug.
issue_context.analysis: This should be a narrow clarification request, not speculative engineering work. The missing information is exactly which PowerToys feature is being described and what state transition is failing to update.
initial_investigation: The issue has no product label and no attachment, which makes it one of the least scoped reports in the batch.
A focused repository search for Wi-Fi status terms did not reveal a single obvious PowerToys surface that matches the report text well enough to assign ownership confidently.

information_gaps.information: Which exact PowerToys feature, page, flyout, or tray surface the reporter means by docking option, and what Wi-Fi status field is expected to update there.
information_gaps.why_needed: This is required to identify the owning module before any fix can be proposed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the exact PowerToys surface name you are looking at when the Wi-Fi status stays stale.

information_gaps.information: A screenshot of the stale Wi-Fi status inside the PowerToys surface the reporter is referring to.
information_gaps.why_needed: A screenshot will reveal whether the report is actually pointing at a PowerToys UI or a different Windows or dock surface.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Capture the affected screen and upload the image through the GitHub web UI, with any private network names removed if needed.

information_gaps.information: The exact transition that should refresh the Wi-Fi status, such as docking, undocking, connecting, disconnecting, or toggling Wi-Fi.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether maintainers should look at a live-status refresh bug, a device-change event, or a misunderstood expected behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with short numbered steps that start from a known state and end at the stale Wi-Fi status.

actions.label: Identify the PowerToys surface and stale Wi-Fi state

comment.body:
Thanks for reporting this. The blocker right now is not a lack of effort from the reporter; it is that the current issue text does not identify which PowerToys feature or UI surface is supposed to show the Wi-Fi status, so maintainers cannot yet route the bug to the right module.

**Needed**
1. Please tell us the exact PowerToys feature, page, flyout, or tray surface you mean by docking option, and what Wi-Fi status should update there.
2. Please upload a screenshot of the stale Wi-Fi status through the GitHub web UI (hide any private network names if needed).
3. Please provide short numbered steps for the transition that should refresh the status, such as docking, undocking, connecting, disconnecting, or toggling Wi-Fi.

That will tell us whether this is a real PowerToys status-refresh bug and which module owns it.
